leah: hi all! i'm leah, just joined eng  quick Q: setting up local dev and not sure whether to use the hosted API key or sandbox. also what's the sandbox rate limit by default?

jon: welcome! for dev use the sandbox key. hosted keys are for prod and billable. sandbox is shared onboarding credits and has modest limits (roughly 50-80 req/min and ~3-5 concurrent connections typical).

support-bot: Reminder: new hire accounts receive a sandbox key automatically. Check Console > Settings > API keys > Sandbox. If missing, run `curl -s https://internal-api.redwood.ai/users/me/keys` (SSO required) or open #help.

leah: thanks! found the key. if i need a temporary bump for a demo tomorrow, how do i request it?

jon: file a quick form on the intranet: https://intranet.redwood.ai/quota-request select "sandbox temporary increase", include expected qps, duration, and contact. DevEx usually approves same day for short demos.

rafa: tip: implement exponential backoff + jitter for 429s, and keep concurrent streaming connections low. Example psuedocode:
```
if (resp.status == 429) wait = base * 2**attempt + jitter; retry();
```

leah: sweet. one last: will sandbox usage show up on org billing? don't want to charge prod cards.

jon: sandbox uses onboarding credits and won't charge your org. heavy or abusive usage may be capped. for production-like testing use a hosted key or request dedicated test capacity.

leah: great, thanks everyone :smile:
